subject: Production p99 spikes during autoscale — urgent
messages:
From: Alice Tang <alice.tang@bluepeak.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: ops@bluepeak.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Production p99 spikes during autoscale — urgent

Hi Jonas,

We started seeing a regression in p95/p99 latency during autoscale events over the last 6 hours. Our charts show p99 jumping from ~420ms to 3.2s during scaleouts; throughput drops and we see a higher 5xx rate coincident with autoscaler activity. This is impacting our live trading pipelines (region us-east-1).

What we observed:
- Time window: 2026-11-29T09:10:00–2026-11-29T09:50:00 (our local TZ)
- p95 stable, p99 spikes only at scale events
- Error samples attached (example request IDs in example_traces.txt)
- We rely on your hosted API; this regression started after the recent runtime patch you shipped on Nov 24.

Can someone on the Redwood side triage? We need an ETA and a mitigation path — this is affecting SLAs and our call center is getting alerts.

Attached: latency_report_20261129.csv, example_traces.txt, trace_screenshot_1623.png

Thanks,
Alice Tang
CTO, BluePeak Analytics

Alice — thanks for the report and the attachments. I’m escalating to our on-call infra lead (Rishi) and CC'ing our CS lead (Marissa) so we can coordinate. Immediate plan:
1) Rishi will triage traces and server-side logs.
2) If needed we'll temporarily pre-warm a small GPU pool to stabilize p99 while we investigate.
3) We’ll follow up with a remediation plan and timeframe.

I’ll update you in 30–45 minutes.

— Jonas Weber

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: alice.tang@bluepeak.com, ops@bluepeak.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production p99 spikes during autoscale — urgent

Taking this on. Initial read of the traces Alice attached: there are long host-side setup times (~1.8–2.4s) on first few requests routed to newly-provisioned GPU workers. Hypothesis: kernel/JIT and model weight page-in costs are dominating cold-starts, and our autoscaler ramp (large step increase) is causing a thundering-herd where many workers enter warmup simultaneously. That aligns with the p99-only degradation.

What I need from BluePeak to confirm:
- A couple of request IDs that hit different worker IPs (you included some in example_traces.txt; thanks — the IDs starting with bp-req- are perfect).
- Any recent change in request size or model variant in use?

Short-term mitigation I'm going to try now (I’ll coordinate with infra team):
- Pre-warm 2 GPU workers pinned to your account for next 2 hours.
- Adjust autoscaler policy to smaller incremental steps (limit scale step to 25% and increase cooldown).

Medium-term: we need to push a runtime improvement (kernel caching + deferred JIT for small helper kernels) to reduce per-worker warmup from ~2s to sub-300ms. I’ll open a JIRA and include timelines.

I’m attaching a quick sampling snippet and will post logs as I correlate.

— Rishi Malhotra
Infra Lead (on-call), Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Attachment: sampling-snippet.txt (stub)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Escalation summary & proposed customer remediation (BluePeak)

Team — summary and ask:

Summary:
- Customer: BluePeak Analytics (critical account, expanding usage)
- Symptom: p99 spikes to multiple seconds during autoscale events; correlated with scaleout bursts
- Root cause (tentative): cold-start warmup overhead on GPU workers + autoscaler step-size causing thundering-herd
- Impact: degraded latency SLAs, increased 5xx during spike windows, customer operations impacted

Immediate remediation proposed (we can do this now):
- Pre-warm 2 GPU workers pinned to BluePeak (target: reduce cold-start to hits on pre-warmed nodes)
- Tweak autoscaler: max scale step 25%, increase cooldown to 90s
- Short communication to customer with mitigation steps and monitoring cadence

Medium-term engineering work (Rishi to own): runtime kernel caching & deferred JIT, automated warm pool for accounts exceeding X rps, and an autoscaler policy that staggers spawn times to avoid synchronized start. Estimate: 3–5 week effort for the runtime patch + staged rollout.

Commercial ask: propose a service credit of 20% for affected windows (Nov 29 09:10–09:50 UTC) given SLA impact; recommend pre-approval so CS can confirm to customer quickly.

Please respond: 1) Approve credits? 2) Any objections to immediate pre-warm & autoscaler tweak? 3) Who from SRE will own the on-call rollout (need at least one SRE + Rishi)?

— Jonas
jonas_weber@redwood.com
